target_condition_opmd_comment: OPMD is represented by carcinoma in situ (CIS) lesions and benign/precancerous oral lesions (e.g., dysplasia, leukoplakia, hyperkeratosis) that were biopsied; CIS showed the same hBD-3 overexpression/hBD-2 underexpression phenotype as OSCC.
target_condition_oscc_comment: OSCC is defined as cancerous oral lesions confirmed by biopsy and pathology review, including invasive squamous cell carcinoma of varying differentiation, staged from CIS through Stage IV; HPV16-induced oropharyngeal carcinoma was also included in a proof-of-concept analysis.
severity_target_condition: Cancer stages among the cancerous subjects: CIS 4%, Stage I 11%, Stage II 17%, Stage III 17%, Stage IV 35%, with 15% information not available.
site_target_condition: Anatomical sites of target lesions in the oral cavity included tongue (36% of cancerous lesions, most frequent site), floor of mouth (FOM, 26%), mandible (11%), buccal mucosa (10%), retromolar trigone (7%), maxilla (3%), hard palate (3%), gingiva (3%), and lip (1%); for benign lesions the distribution included tongue (42%), buccal (23%), lip (12%), soft palate (7%), gingiva (5%), hard palate (5%), mandibular ridge (3%), hamular notch (2%), and lingual to #14 (2%).

target_condition_opmd_comment: OPMD is defined as OPMD subtypes/histopathological categories: keratosis with no dysplasia, genuine OLP and OLL without dysplasia, low-risk OED, and high-risk OED (using the binary grading system for dysplasia).
target_condition_oscc_comment: OSCC is defined as a single diagnostic category (oral squamous cell carcinoma) among the five histopathological groups; no further differentiation grade or TNM staging subtypes were specified.
severity_target_condition: Severity spectrum spans keratosis without dysplasia, OLP/OLL without dysplasia, low-risk OED, high-risk OED (binary grading system, with carcinoma in situ merged into high-risk OED), and OSCC. site_target_condition: Lesions occurred across multiple oral cavity sites, most commonly labial/buccal mucosa (34.2%) followed by lateral surface of the tongue (27.1%), with additional sites including alveolar ridge/palate and floor of mouth.
